anomalies.observed: On the EPD_Driver sheet C2 is drawn with the value 1 nF / 6.3 V (the 6.3 V rating matches the reference part, but the capacitance is three orders of magnitude low).
anomalies.expected: The spec states the Meshinger schematic uses the PDI 'G1 group only' value for this capacitor, i.e. C2 = 1 µF / 6.3 V.

evidence.quote: EPD_Driver sheet: 'C2' with value '1nF/6.3V' next to L1/Display_Power_Switch
C1 (G1 group only): 1 µF/6.3 V | C2 = 1 µF/6.3 V | Matches G1-specific value

anomalies.impact: A 1000x-too-small capacitor on the EPD boost/charge-pump supply node would severely degrade the panel's storage/decoupling and could stop the boost converter from regulating the panel high-voltage rails, leaving the display blank.

anomalies.observed: On the EPD_Driver sheet C1 is drawn with the value 0.1 µF / 16 V.
anomalies.expected: Per the spec this position belongs to the PDI 'C2 default' group, which should be 1 µF / 25 V.

evidence.quote: EPD_Driver sheet: 'C1' with value '0.1uF/16V' beside L1/Display_Power_Switch
C2 default: 1 µF/25 V | C1/C5/C7/C8/C9/C10 = 1 µF/25 V | Matches default

anomalies.impact: A 10x-low capacitance and a lower voltage rating (16 V vs 25 V) on the EPD supply decoupling reduces boost stability/margin and derates the part below the intended rail.

parsed.summary: The EPD driver sheet's capacitor values deviate from the intended design: C2 is a 1 nF/6.3 V part where the spec calls for 1 µF/6.3 V, and C1 is 0.1 µF/16 V where the spec calls for 1 µF/25 V. Both are in the EPD boost/charge-pump supply, so the e-paper display would not be driven as intended.
